title: Oakden Healthcare teletriage LLM oncall scratchpad
content:
Call notes (2025-02-11):
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood), Rafael (Redwood SE), Dr. Ana Park (Oakden PM), Priya (Oakden infra), Samir (Oakden security).
- Goal: quick feasibility check for deploying a patient-facing triage assistant in their existing EHR VPC (air-gapped-ish).
- High-level ask: short-response triage flows + clinical guidance summarization + structured outputs (ICD-ish tags, urgency: low/med/high). Must be auditable.

Key non-functional constraints:
- Data residency: PHI must not leave customer VPC. Oakden wants Private deployment (customer-managed control plane + on-prem inference).
- KMS/HSM: on-prem HSM for encryption keys; integration with Azure Key Vault HSM is preferred.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 450ms for single-turn triage prompts (expected avg tokens per response ~120).
- Throughput: 15 QPS steady during clinic peaks, burst to 35 QPS for 60s windows.
- Offline/edge fallback: if inference nodes unhealthy, fallback to a lightweight decision-tree (customer-provided) hosted inside same VPC.

Technical notes / gotchas we surfaced:
- EHR payloads are heavy (lots of structured JSON). Recommend pre-extracting only relevant fields server-side before sending to Redwood runtime to avoid token bloat.
- Session affinity: Oakden uses patient session attachments; need sticky routing to keep KV cache warm per active patient session. Ask: can we pin cache by session-id? (Maya: Redwood runtime supports per-session KV with configurable TTL and memory cap; documentation link to include).
- Tokenization differences: their legacy symptom codes will be embedded in prompts; warn about embedding OOV tokens and token counts. Suggest using embeddings + retrieval for long patient history, not conditioning full history into prompt.
- Safety/regulatory: outputs must include provenance header (model id + timestamp + confidence heuristic). Customer wants audit log export on-demand.

Model/qualitative preferences:
- They prefer an Llama-family variant that runs well in quantized FP16/8 on A100 equivalently sized fleet. They asked about Redwood-verified models; we should propose 2 model variants: one low-latency smaller quantized model for triage + a higher-quality larger model for free-text summarization.
- Request: evaluation harness to compare hallucination rate on 200 sampled triage cases (we should propose prompt-suite + scoring rubrics).

Operational asks from Priya (infra):
- How will rolling restarts affect in-flight patient sessions? Need clear guidance about graceful drain and fallback routing.
- Network: only outbound to Redwood control plane on 443 allowed; they need a list of IPs and domains for provisioning. Also require mTLS between control plane and their private agent.
- Resource planning: estimate GPU count. Quick calc: at 120 tokens/response, 15 sustained QPS, batching factor expected 3 -> ~5400 tokens/s. Need approximate vGPU hours: ask infra team to run perf test; Redwood to provide benchmark across model variants.

Open questions to resolve:
1) Can we deliver audit-log export to their SIEM in a HIPAA-friendly format? (Samir follow-up)
2) Required retention policy for KV caches and logs (legal asks 7 years for some triage records?).
3) Precise failure-mode SLA they want for dedicated vs private — can we offer a hybrid: private inference + hosted control plane? (they indicated this is acceptable).
4) Will embedding store be hosted by Oakden or by Redwood in their VPC? They prefer Oakden-managed to avoid egress.

Action items / next steps (owners):
- Rafael: prepare an initial model/quantization recommendation doc and perf matrix (due 2025-02-18).
- Maya: draft a short runbook for session sticky routing and graceful drain patterns (due 2025-02-14).
- Priya: share network ACL template and exact firewall rules they can open for us; ask for IP allowlist (due 2025-02-13).
- Samir: confirm legal retention windows and PHI policy constraints and share sample DPA redlines (due 2025-02-21).
- Oakden: provide 200 anonymized triage transcripts for initial eval (deliver by 2025-02-28).

Rough prompt sketches (for eval):
- System: "You are a clinician-facing triage assistant. Classify urgency and provide a concise plan. Always include an explanation and cite patient symptoms."
- User: short patient complaint + vitals array (we will test noise and missing fields).
- Desired structured output: JSON with fields: {severity_level, icd_tags[], short_summary, recommended_action, confidence_score, provenance}.

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc messy — capture follow-ups from Slack thread #oakden-triage (link above).
- Watch for scope creep: Oakden keeps asking for multi-lingual and phone-voice integration; scope to stage 2.
- Consider proposing Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching + prefix cache rules to hit their latency targets without doubling GPU fleet.

Meeting snippets / friction points:
- Dr. Ana: worried about hallucinations; asked for thresholding and human-in-the-loop escalation paths.
- Priya: strongly prefers their own embedding store. Must validate our SDK supports S3-compatible endpoints for vector store.

Quick sketches of handoffs:
- Sales -> SE: attach JIRA OT-4123, include legal intake ticket and SOC2/HIPAA checklist.
- SE -> Eng (private deploy team): raise infra spike to validate mTLS agent and per-session KV TTL.

Endnotes:
- Keep tone conservative: prioritize auditability and minimal hallucination risk. Next sync: 2025-02-18 (perf write-up review).

Raw scratch logs (copied from Slack thread):
- "If we push full EHR notes into prompt, token cost explodes — need retrieval + embed" — Priya 02/10
- "Can we do deterministic fallbacks to decision-tree inside VPC?" — Dr. Ana 02/11
- "Legal: redline DPA to add HSM language + 7yr retention question" — Samir 02/12

-- end of scratchpad --
